correctness.rationale: For the one-sided period-doubling fixed point µ(0)=01, µ(1)=00, all even positions are zero; hence all factors of length >=2 contain a zero and each µ-image has at least one one only at odd positions. Every length-2n factor begins in even or odd substitution phase, and an odd-phase factor is a single-letter cyclic rotation of an aligned µ-image, proving surjectivity. A conjugating odd rotation between µ-images would move a one to an impossible even position, so conjugacy shifts are even and descend to source-word rotations by injectivity of µ. n=1 has two distinct image classes. Thus Φ_n is bijective for every n and c(2^k m)=c(m) for all k>=0. Independently enumerated literal cyclic classes for n=1..48 with morphic images matched; this finite check is not the universal argument.
